   101	h2_mean <- fit_h2(ci_A, mods = ~ 1)$model
   102	h2 <- fit_h2(ci_A)
   103	h2_coef <- function(m, term = "extremity") {
   104	  i <- which(rownames(m$beta) == term)
   105	  c(est = m$beta[i], lo = m$ci.lb[i], hi = m$ci.ub[i], p = m$pval[i])
   106	}
   107	s2 <- h2_coef(h2$model)
   108	h2_tab <- data.table(n_cells = nrow(ci_A), n_studies = uniqueN(ci_A$study), n_rows = nrow(drop_gross_errors(A)),
   109	                     mean_ai = h2_mean$beta[1], mean_ai_lo = h2_mean$ci.lb, mean_ai_hi = h2_mean$ci.ub,
   110	                     slope = s2[["est"]], slope_lo = s2[["lo"]], slope_hi = s2[["hi"]], slope_p = s2[["p"]],
   111	                     robust_fallback = h2$robust_fallback)
   112	h2_tab[, verdict := shape_verdict(mean_ai_lo, slope_lo, slope_hi, slope_lo, slope_hi, slope_bounds)]
   113	
   114	# ---- H3: model adequacy ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   115	pi <- fread(file.path("output", "predictive_intervals.csv"))
   116	obs <- list(g = h1$pooled$g, rho = h1$pooled$rho, slope = h2_tab$slope)
   117	h3_tab <- pi[, .(model,
   118	                 g_inside = obs$g >= g_lo & obs$g <= g_hi,
   119	                 rho_inside = obs$rho >= rho_lo & obs$rho <= rho_hi,
   120	                 slope_inside = obs$slope >= slope_lo & obs$slope <= slope_hi,
   121	                 b_inside = h1$pooled$b >= b_lo & h1$pooled$b <= b_hi,
   122	                 mean_ai_inside = h2_tab$mean_ai >= ai_lo & h2_tab$mean_ai <= ai_hi)]
   123	# Shape criteria decide survival; level criteria (b, mean index) depend on the calibration to
   124	# Jacowitz & Kahneman and are reported separately. M0 is also contradicted when gate G1 passes.
   125	h3_tab[, survives_shape := (g_inside | rho_inside) & slope_inside]
   126	h3_tab[model == "M0", survives_shape := survives_shape & h1$pooled$b_ci[1] <= 0]
   127	h3_tab[, survives_level := b_inside & mean_ai_inside]
   128	
   129	# ---- Robustness (Q24) ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   130	rob <- list()
   131	# R1: median regression without the gross-error rule, participant-cluster bootstrap
   132	{
   133	  d <- copy(W)[, xx := x * abs(x)]
   134	  f <- y ~ 0 + factor(cell) + factor(cell):x + xx
   135	  est <- coef(rq(f, tau = 0.5, data = d))["xx"]
   136	  pids <- unique(d$pid)
   137	  set.seed(20260927)
   138	  boot <- replicate(if (dry_run) 100 else 1000, {
   139	    s <- data.table(pid = sample(pids, replace = TRUE))[, draw := .I]
   140	    bd <- d[s, on = "pid", allow.cartesian = TRUE]
   141	    tryCatch(coef(rq(f, tau = 0.5, data = bd))["xx"], error = function(e) NA_real_)
   142	  })
   143	  rob$R1_median_regression_g <- c(est = unname(est), lo = unname(quantile(boot, .025, na.rm = TRUE)), hi = unname(quantile(boot, .975, na.rm = TRUE)))
   144	}
   145	# R2: piecewise slopes, knot at |x| = 1
   146	{
   147	  d <- drop_gross_errors(W)[, h := sign(x) * pmax(abs(x) - 1, 0)]
   148	  m <- lmerTest::lmer(y ~ x + h + (1 + x + h || cell) + (1 | pid), data = d)
   149	  co <- summary(m)$coefficients
   150	  rob$R2_far_minus_near_slope <- c(est = co["h", "Estimate"], lo = co["h", "Estimate"] - qt(.975, co["h", "df"]) * co["h", "Std. Error"],
   151	                                   hi = co["h", "Estimate"] + qt(.975, co["h", "df"]) * co["h", "Std. Error"])
   152	}
   153	# R3: without Bahník (2021a)
   154	{
   155	  f3 <- fit_h1(W[reference_short != "Bahník, 2021a"])
   156	  rob$R3_without_bahnik_g <- c(est = f3$g, lo = f3$g_ci[1], hi = f3$g_ci[2])
   157	}
   158	# R4: raw-scale anchoring index
   159	{
   160	  r <- merge(drop_gross_errors(A)[, .(cell, anchorhigh, est)], cells_A[, .(cell, study, a_low, a_high, extremity)], by = "cell")
   161	  ci4 <- r[, .(ai = (median(est[anchorhigh == 1]) - median(est[anchorhigh == 0])) / (a_high[1] - a_low[1]),
   162	               ai_se = 1.2533 * sqrt(mad(est[anchorhigh == 1])^2 / sum(anchorhigh == 1) + mad(est[anchorhigh == 0])^2 / sum(anchorhigh == 0)) / (a_high[1] - a_low[1]),
   163	               study = study[1], extremity = extremity[1]), by = cell][ai_se > 0]
   164	  rob$R4_raw_index_slope <- h2_coef(fit_h2(ci4)$model)
   165	}
   166	# R5: covariates
   167	{
   168	  cov <- unique(sets$across_rows[, .(cell, anchortype = factor(anchortype), comparative_question, direction,
   169	                                     incentive_any = as.integer(incentive != 0), experiment_type = factor(experiment_type))], by = "cell")
   170	  ci5 <- merge(ci_A, cov, by = "cell")
   171	  keep <- names(which(sapply(ci5[, .(anchortype, comparative_question, direction, incentive_any, experiment_type)], uniqueN) > 1))
   172	  rob$R5_covariates_slope <- h2_coef(fit_h2(ci5, mods = reformulate(c("extremity", keep)))$model)
   173	}
   174	# R6: without Weber et al. (2021)
   175	rob$R6_without_weber_slope <- h2_coef(fit_h2(ci_A[study != "Weber et al., 2021"])$model)
   176	# R7: alternative extremity measures
   177	{
   178	  ci7 <- copy(ci_A)[, `:=`(ext_max = pmax(abs(x_low), abs(x_high)), ext_spread = x_high - x_low)]
   179	  rob$R7_max_distance_slope <- h2_coef(fit_h2(ci7, mods = ~ ext_max)$model, "ext_max")
   180	  rob$R7_log_spread_slope <- h2_coef(fit_h2(ci7, mods = ~ ext_spread)$model, "ext_spread")
   181	}
   182	rob_tab <- rbindlist(lapply(names(rob), function(k) data.table(analysis = k, est = rob[[k]][1], lo = rob[[k]][2], hi = rob[[k]][3])))
   183	
   184	# ---- Save ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   185	fwrite(exclusions, file.path(out_dir, "exclusions.csv"))
   186	fwrite(h1_tab, file.path(out_dir, "h1_within.csv"))
   187	fwrite(h2_tab, file.path(out_dir, "h2_across.csv"))
   188	fwrite(ci_A, file.path(out_dir, "h2_cell_indices.csv"))
   189	fwrite(h3_tab, file.path(out_dir, "h3_model_adequacy.csv"))
   190	fwrite(rob_tab, file.path(out_dir, "robustness.csv"))
   191	saveRDS(list(h1 = h1, h2 = h2, h2_mean = h2_mean, W = W, A = A, ci_A = ci_A), file.path(out_dir, "fits.rds"))
   192	print(exclusions); print(h1_tab); print(h2_tab); print(h3_tab); print(rob_tab)

### run_all.sh
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Rerun the whole study from the raw data: ./run_all.sh
     3	# Steps 02-03 regenerate the model predictions (about 15 minutes on 8 cores); they are
     4	# deterministic, so the rerun reproduces the preregistered predictions.
     5	set -euo pipefail
     6	cd "$(dirname "$0")"
     7	Rscript R/00_fetch.R                  # download OpAQ and verify its SHA-256
     8	Rscript R/01_design_inventory.R       # design-only inventory (no estimates)
     9	Rscript R/02_calibrate_models.R       # calibrate models to Jacowitz & Kahneman (1995)
    10	Rscript R/03_simulate_predictions.R   # model predictions on the OpAQ designs
    11	Rscript R/03b_decision_properties.R   # operating characteristics of the decision rules
    12	Rscript R/03c_prereg_tables.R         # prediction tables used in the preregistration
    13	Rscript R/04_confirmatory.R           # preregistered confirmatory analyses

prereg/preregistration.md:31:- H1 (within-item curvature, pooled): under M1 the curvature g is positive (median 0.062, 95% predictive interval [0.030, 0.095]); under M2 it is zero (0.000 [-0.007, 0.007]; rho [-0.017, 0.016]); under M3 and M4 it is negative (M3: -0.046 [-0.071, -0.022]; M4: -0.066 [-0.110, -0.017]). M1R makes no determinate sign prediction: its curvature depends on its parameters (0.003 [-0.029, 0.082]). Under M0 the average elasticity b is zero, so the shape is undefined.
prereg/preregistration.md:50:**Q11. Manipulated variables.** The anchor value (`anchor`), its side (`anchorhigh`: 1 high, 0 low), and its type (`anchortype`: 1 explicitly random, 2 fixed without explanation, 3 relevant to the target). x = ln(anchor / true value).
prereg/preregistration.md:55:- Across-cell anchoring index for a cell with one low anchor A_L and one high anchor A_H: AI = [median(y | high) - median(y | low)] / [ln(A_H) - ln(A_L)]. Extremity of the cell: E = (|x_L| + |x_H|) / 2, the mean absolute log distance of the two anchors from the true value.
prereg/preregistration.md:58:Rows enter only if: `anchortype` is 1, 2 or 3 (excludes self-generated and incidental anchors); `scaletype` = 1 (open response); `tasktype` is a positive ratio-scale quantity (quantity, number, price, length, height, distance, weight, population, volume, speed, duration, birth rate, income, width, area, circumference, age); anchor and true value are numeric and positive; the study is not Röseler & Wagner (2021), whose anchors were computed from each participant's own unanchored estimates. The true value of a cell is the value on its first row.
prereg/preregistration.md:64:**Q15. Outliers.** Gross errors (unit errors, typing slips) are removed with one rule applied identically to simulated and observed data (`drop_gross_errors()` in `R/estimators.R`): a response is dropped when |y| exceeds both ln(1000) and the cell's largest |x| plus ln(10). A response equal to any anchor is always retained. No other trimming. Robustness analysis R1 uses median regression without this rule.
prereg/preregistration.md:74:- Columns read (design only, via `R/read_opaq.R`): reference_short, reference, id, participant_id, sex, age, nationality, anchoring_item, true_value, anchor, anchorhigh, anchortype, tasktype, direction, incentive, comparative_question, experiment_type, stimulitype, sampletype, scaletype, published, preregistered. Outputs seen: `output/design_inventory.txt`, `output/design_cells.csv`, and the cell and row counts in Q13.
prereg/preregistration.md:86:H2. Across-cell set: AI and its SE per cell (SE of each median = 1.2533 × MAD / sqrt(n)); multilevel meta-regression (metafor rma.mv, REML) of AI on E with random intercepts for study and cell within study. Estimate: slope d.
prereg/preregistration.md:100:Cells are medians with 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles across replicates, generated by `R/03c_prereg_tables.R` (`output/prereg_tables.md`, `output/predictive_intervals.csv`). The simulation estimator always fits the full random-effects structure with lme4; the confirmatory analysis uses the same formula in lmerTest with the Q23 fallback. Other fixed simulation assumptions (`R/models.R`): SD of belief centres across people 0.6 sigma; response noise 0.3 sigma; person offset SD 0.15; 2% of responses contaminated with N(0, 2) log-unit errors. M1R additionally has kappa, the agent's own uncertainty relative to the spread of beliefs across people (0.25-1; only 0.25-0.75 reproduce the benchmark). Calibration grid and accepted values: `output/calibration_grid.csv`.
prereg/preregistration.md:131:- H3: a model is contradicted by a statistic when the observed point estimate lies outside that model's 95% predictive interval. Shape criterion (decides survival): a model survives if the observed g or rho, and the observed d, lie inside its intervals; M0 is also contradicted whenever gate G1 passes. Level criterion (reported, does not decide survival): observed b and mean log anchoring index inside the model's intervals. Levels depend on the calibration to Jacowitz & Kahneman's anchors and task, which need not transfer to OpAQ designs; shapes follow from model structure. We report which models survive; if none survives, we say so.
prereg/preregistration.md:134:**Q23. Analytic problems.** If the H1 model fails to converge or is singular, we remove random-effect terms in this order until it converges: curvature variance, slope variance; the participant intercept is kept. If rma.mv fails, we fit a single-level random-effects meta-regression with study-clustered robust SEs (clubSandwich if available, otherwise metafor::robust). Any such change is reported in `deviations.md`.
prereg/preregistration.md:137:- R1: median regression (quantreg, tau = .5) of y on cell-specific intercepts and slopes plus a common x|x| term, without the gross-error rule; CI by participant-cluster bootstrap (1,000 draws).
prereg/preregistration.md:140:- R4: H2 with raw-scale anchoring index (Jacowitz & Kahneman, 1995): [median(estimate | high) - median(estimate | low)] / (A_H - A_L). Descriptive only: the models are specified on the log scale, and a dry run with data simulated from M2 gave a raw-scale slope of -0.07 [-0.11, -0.02], so a falling raw-scale index does not discriminate between models.

prereg/preregistration.md:50:**Q11. Manipulated variables.** The anchor value (`anchor`), its side (`anchorhigh`: 1 high, 0 low), and its type (`anchortype`: 1 explicitly random, 2 fixed without explanation, 3 relevant to the target). x = ln(anchor / true value).
prereg/preregistration.md:55:- Across-cell anchoring index for a cell with one low anchor A_L and one high anchor A_H: AI = [median(y | high) - median(y | low)] / [ln(A_H) - ln(A_L)]. prereg/preregistration.md:58:Rows enter only if: `anchortype` is 1, 2 or 3 (excludes self-generated and incidental anchors); `scaletype` = 1 (open response); `tasktype` is a positive ratio-scale quantity (quantity, number, price, length, height, distance, weight, population, volume, speed, duration, birth rate, income, width, area, circumference, age); anchor and true value are numeric and positive; the study is not Röseler & Wagner (2021), whose anchors were computed from each participant's own unanchored estimates. The true value of a cell is the value on its first row.
prereg/preregistration.md:64:**Q15. Outliers.** Gross errors (unit errors, typing slips) are removed with one rule applied identically to simulated and observed data (`drop_gross_errors()` in `R/estimators.R`): a response is dropped when |y| exceeds both ln(1000) and the cell's largest |x| plus ln(10). A response equal to any anchor is always retained. No other trimming. Robustness analysis R1 uses median regression without this rule.
prereg/preregistration.md:74:- Columns read (design only, via `R/read_opaq.R`): reference_short, reference, id, participant_id, sex, age, nationality, anchoring_item, true_value, anchor, anchorhigh, anchortype, tasktype, direction, incentive, comparative_question, experiment_type, stimulitype, sampletype, scaletype, published, preregistered. prereg/preregistration.md:86:H2. Across-cell set: AI and its SE per cell (SE of each median = 1.2533 × MAD / sqrt(n)); multilevel meta-regression (metafor rma.mv, REML) of AI on E with random intercepts for study and cell within study. Estimate: slope d.
prereg/preregistration.md:100:Cells are medians with 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles across replicates, generated by `R/03c_prereg_tables.R` (`output/prereg_tables.md`, `output/predictive_intervals.csv`). The simulation estimator always fits the full random-effects structure with lme4; the confirmatory analysis uses the same formula in lmerTest with the Q23 fallback. Other fixed simulation assumptions (`R/models.R`): SD of belief centres across people 0.6 sigma; response noise 0.3 sigma; person offset SD 0.15; 2% of responses contaminated with N(0, 2) log-unit errors. M1R additionally has kappa, the agent's own uncertainty relative to the spread of beliefs across people (0.25-1; only 0.25-0.75 reproduce the benchmark). Calibration grid and accepted values: `output/calibration_grid.csv`.
prereg/preregistration.md:131:- H3: a model is contradicted by a statistic when the observed point estimate lies outside that model's 95% predictive interval. Shape criterion (decides survival): a model survives if the observed g or rho, and the observed d, lie inside its intervals; M0 is also contradicted whenever gate G1 passes. Level criterion (reported, does not decide survival): observed b and mean log anchoring index inside the model's intervals. Levels depend on the calibration to Jacowitz & Kahneman's anchors and task, which need not transfer to OpAQ designs; shapes follow from model structure. We report which models survive; if none survives, we say so.
prereg/preregistration.md:134:**Q23. Analytic problems.** If the H1 model fails to converge or is singular, we remove random-effect terms in this order until it converges: curvature variance, slope variance; the participant intercept is kept. If rma.mv fails, we fit a single-level random-effects meta-regression with study-clustered robust SEs (clubSandwich if available, otherwise metafor::robust). Any such change is reported in `deviations.md`.
prereg/preregistration.md:137:- R1: median regression (quantreg, tau = .5) of y on cell-specific intercepts and slopes plus a common x|x| term, without the gross-error rule; CI by participant-cluster bootstrap (1,000 draws).
prereg/preregistration.md:140:- R4: H2 with raw-scale anchoring index (Jacowitz & Kahneman, 1995): [median(estimate | high) - median(estimate | low)] / (A_H - A_L). content.text: A raw-data check found that 870 of the 987 across-cell “gross errors” come from one item: Chicago population responses are recorded as values around 2–5 while its truth and anchors are in whole persons. The registered rule therefore drops that entire cell. I also found that the external benchmark uses a raw-scale index, while the calibration code computes a log-scale index; that affects how the model predictions should be interpreted.

A raw-data check found that 870 of the 987 across-cell “gross errors” come from one item: Chicago population responses are recorded as values around 2–5 while its truth and anchors are in whole persons. The registered rule therefore drops that entire cell. I also found that the external benchmark uses a raw-scale index, while the calibration code computes a log-scale index; that affects how the model predictions should be interpreted.

## Answer

**The registered decision rules produce the committed headline verdicts:** pooled H1 is *falling*, H1a is *falling*, H1b fails its anchoring gate, H2 is *inconclusive*, and M1R is the sole H3 shape survivor. Several implementation and data issues limit what those verdicts establish. The most consequential are the external calibration scale, the H3 level-estimator mismatch, and the dependence of H1 on one study.

The [preregistration](~/Documents/Coding/ai-jdm-paper/prereg/preregistration.md:5) and frozen predictions are in tag `prereg-v1` at `a40911b` (22:56 BST); the confirmatory outputs are in the next commit, `14ec907` (22:58 BST). The local raw file matches the full SHA-256 recorded in the preregistration.

### MAJOR

- **The external benchmark is calibrated on the wrong scale.** [models.R](~/Documents/Coding/ai-jdm-paper/R/models.R:94) computes `(median(log response at high) − median(log response at low)) / log anchor spread`. The preregistration calls the Jacowitz–Kahneman index a **raw-scale** quantity in [Q24](~/Documents/Coding/ai-jdm-paper/prereg/preregistration.md:140), yet [calibration](~/Documents/Coding/ai-jdm-paper/R/02_calibrate_models.R:9) accepts parameters using this log-scale value and the external .30–.60 band. Those indices are not generally equal. Recompute the benchmark on the raw scale, then regenerate the accepted parameter sets and predictive intervals. Treat changes to the frozen predictions as a documented post-preregistration sensitivity analysis.

- **M1R’s `kappa` does not have its stated meaning.** [models.R](~/Documents/Coding/ai-jdm-paper/R/models.R:75) calls it uncertainty relative to the *spread of beliefs across people*, but uses `kappa * sigma`; that spread is `0.6 * sigma` in [the same file](~/Documents/Coding/ai-jdm-paper/R/models.R:9). If the stated definition is intended, the target SD should be `kappa * 0.6 * sigma`. This changes the parameter region that passes calibration and may change M1R’s broad predictions. Correct and rerun it, or correct the model description and justify the chosen range.

- **H3 compares different estimators for its level criterion.** Simulation [fit_across()](~/Documents/Coding/ai-jdm-paper/R/estimators.R:44) records an inverse-sampling-variance weighted mean AI; observed [H2/H3](~/Documents/Coding/ai-jdm-paper/R/04_confirmatory.R:101) use the intercept of an intercept-only multilevel model. From the committed cell indices, the former is **0.241**, versus the reported latter **0.416**. Using 0.241 would reverse the `mean_ai_inside` flags for M2 and M4 and make M4’s reported *level* criterion pass. It does **not** change preregistered shape survival. Apply the same estimator to simulated and observed data and regenerate the H3 level columns.

- **The H1 inference has limited independent study support.** The pooled [H1 result](~/Documents/Coding/ai-jdm-paper/output/confirmatory/h1_within.csv:2) is \(g=-0.0406\), 95% CI \([-0.0582,-0.0231]\), with Satterthwaite df **9.10**. Thirteen of 20 cells come from Bahník (2021a); [the model](~/Documents/Coding/ai-jdm-paper/R/04_confirmatory.R:55) has cell and participant effects but no study-level effect. Registered R3, excluding Bahník, gives \(-0.0450\), CI \([-0.358,0.268]\). Report the pooled finding as evidence for these sampled cells, with study dependence prominent; add a clearly labelled study-level or leave-one-study-out sensitivity analysis before generalising the shape.
